cases.title: Apia Park stadium rehabilitation: a worker killed and two hurt moving beams
cases.place: Apia Park sports complex, Apia, Samoa
cases.point: Apia Park sports complex (OpenStreetMap way 666117780), the coordinate AidData's own location narrative gives for the project. The accident happened on the stadium works at that site.

lenders.name: China Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
lenders.role: AidData record 64861. This was a grant, not a loan: RMB 43,000,000 ($6,900,000) provided to the Government of Samoa on 28 March 2005 for the Apia Park Stadium Rehabilitation Project, which AidData values at $11,389,289 in constant 2021 dollars. MOFCOM was the project sponsor, carried out the final project inspection on 12 March 2007, and the works were handed over to the Samoan authorities on 3 April 2007. The same record notes that the interest-free Chinese loan which had financed the original stadium, built between 1981 and 1983 for the 1983 South Pacific Games, was forgiven in 2006. No World Bank P-number exists for this financing.

cases.conditions: The grant was spent through a Chinese contractor rather than paid to Samoa to procure with: a project design contract was signed in early 2005 at a ceremony attended by Prime Minister Tuilaepa, Samoa's Minister of Engineering, the Chinese ambassador Liu Guanren and the head of the Economic and Commercial Office, Zhou Geping, and on 13 December 2005 a project implementation contract was signed with Qingjian Group, which AidData says was then called Qingdao Construction Group Corporation. Groundbreaking was on 17 February 2006 and the Chinese ministry that provided the money also signed off the finished works. AidData's own record names the contractor two ways: its description names Qingjian Group (then Qingdao Construction Group Corporation), while its implementing-agency field reads "Chongqing Construction Engineering Group|Government of Samoa". RNZ Pacific spells the contractor Qindao Construction Group Ltd (AidData record 64861; RNZ Pacific).

companies.name: Qingjian Group (formerly Qingdao Construction Group Corporation)
companies.role: Held the project implementation contract signed on 13 December 2005 and was carrying out the stadium works when the fatal accident happened. RNZ Pacific spells the name Qindao Construction Group Ltd and gives its general manager as Hai Wang

cases.community: Samoa asked China to repair and expand the stadium so that it could host the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2007 South Pacific Games. The works reinforced the stands, renovated a runway, added stands, VIP boxes and tennis courts (AidData record 64861). In February 2007, during those works, a worker was killed and two others were hurt. AidData's record says a Chinese engineer was killed when he fell from a machine being used to install beams for the stadium, that a second Chinese engineer was hospitalised after being severely injured in the same incident, and that a Samoan worker was also injured. RNZ Pacific, reporting on a claim that the deaths were being covered up, says a Chinese man was killed and two other workers injured in an incident "in February" during construction of the stadium, and that the Games organisers' account of the accident has a beam being moved during the works when it happened. Leulua'ialii Olinda Woodroffe, a New Zealand-based Samoan lawyer, said someone was trying to cover the incident up, and that Qindao Construction Group Ltd had hired her to investigate the death and the injuries. The chief executive of the South Pacific Games, Fonoti Manogiamanu Etuale, said police had thoroughly investigated the incident and that "there has been no cover up of the death of the Chinese worker"; he said the construction company's general manager, Hai Wang, had told him the lawyer was hired to help recover an insurance claim on a damaged beam that was being moved when the fatal accident happened (RNZ Pacific). Neither source names the dead man, and neither gives a day in February.
cases.killed_note: One worker killed on the stadium works. AidData has a Chinese engineer killed by a fall from a machine installing beams, with a second Chinese engineer hospitalised with severe injuries and a Samoan worker also injured; RNZ Pacific has one Chinese man killed and two other workers injured. The dead man is not named in either source, and the two injuries are counted nowhere as a figure of their own.
cases.outcome: The Chinese ministry that funded the works carried out its final inspection on 12 March 2007, five weeks or so after the accident, and the stadium was handed over to the Samoan authorities on 3 April 2007 and used for the Games that year (AidData record 64861). The Games chief executive said police had investigated the death thoroughly; no police, coroner's or labour-inspection finding on it is held here, and whether the dead man's family or the injured men were paid anything is not established, beyond the Games chief executive's account that the lawyer's instructions concerned an insurance claim on the damaged beam (RNZ Pacific). AidData records a later controversy over the complex: citing the Lowy Institute and several media reports, it says Samoa could not meet the recurring cost of maintaining the swimming pool at the Aquatic Centre and asked New Zealand to carry it.

sources.title: Lawyer claims cover-up over death at Samoa's South Pacific Games stadium project; Games chief executive says police investigated thoroughly
AidData Global Chinese Development Finance Dataset, record 64861: Chinese Government provides RMB 43 million grant for Apia Park Stadium Rehabilitation Project
Cablegate: Chinese Growing Investments in Samoa (Wellington 000773)

cases.confidence_note: The death is carried outside AidData by one source: an RNZ Pacific report of a lawyer's cover-up claim and the Games chief executive's answer to it, which gives one man killed, two workers injured, the contractor's name and a beam being moved during the works when the fatal accident happened. That page carries no date and says only "in February"; February 2007 is AidData's date, not the report's. AidData's record is the only place here that gives the fall from a beam-installing machine, the second engineer's hospitalisation and the Samoan worker's injury; the 2007 Pacific Islands Report article it cites for them, "1 DEAD, 2 HURT IN APIA GAMES PROJECT ACCIDENT", is not held here. The two sources also spell the contractor differently, and AidData's own implementing-agency field names a different company again, so which firm employed the dead man is not settled. The US embassy cable of 25 October 2007 confirms only the Chinese financing of the Games venues and the forgiveness of the loans; it says nothing about the accident. No inquiry finding and no compensation record is held here.
cx: Chinese government grant for the Apia Park stadium rehabilitation
cases.whole: The grant paid for the main venue of the 2007 South Pacific Games: reinforced stands, a renovated runway, extra stands, VIP boxes and tennis courts at a complex China had built in the first place, between 1981 and 1983, with an interest-free loan for the 1983 Games, and had funded a run of maintenance and renovation projects on since. That loan was forgiven in 2006. Samoa then could not meet the running costs of what it had been given: AidData, citing the Lowy Institute and several media reports, says the government could not finance the recurring cost of maintaining the Aquatic Centre swimming pool and asked New Zealand to shoulder it (AidData record 64861).

codesc.name: AVIC International Holding Corporation
codesc.desc: Chinese company registered in Beijing whose business, as its entry on the UK register of overseas companies states it, is international aviation, trade and logistics, and real estate and hotel management. The same register records it under the former name China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation up to 25 October 2010.

sources.title: Company Overview for AVIC INTERNATIONAL HOLDING CORPORATION (FC028179)

codesc.note: Opened the Companies House overseas-company record FC028179. It gives the name exactly as the case key has it, country of incorporation CHINA, legal form Limited, home registry the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the PRC, overseas address 'Avic Intl.Plaza/No.18, Beichen East Rd, Chaoyang District, Beijing 100101, China', objects 'International aviation, trade and logistic, real estate & hotels management', and the previous name China National Aero-Technology Import & Export Corporation for the period 01 Nov 2007 - 25 Oct 2010. Deliberately not written: that it is state-owned, or a subsidiary of Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC). No page I opened says either of the company in the key; the Air University/CASI page on AVIC's organisation failed at its own site (client_error through WebFetch), and the Hong Kong-listed AVIC International Holdings Limited is a different entity, which is fault 2. The register gives no incorporation date and no size figure, so none is given. The '25 Oct 2010' date is the end of the former-name period in the UK record, not a dated statement that the company was renamed in China that day, and it is written that way.

codesc.name: Shanghai Municipal Engineering Design Institute (Group) Co., Ltd
codesc.desc: Engineering design firm in Shanghai. Engineering News-Record's 2017 ranking of Chinese design firms placed it 12th by total design revenue, at $367.13 million; the list does not say which year that revenue covers.
codesc.note: Opened ENR's 2017 Top Chinese Design Firms table. Its row reads '12 | 12 | Shanghai Municipal Engineering Design Institute (Group) Co. Ltd., Shanghai | $367.13' under the headings '2017 Rank', '2016 Rank', 'Company Name, City, Province' and 'Total Design Revenue' (in millions of dollars). So the sector classification is ENR's, not a reading of the name, and Shanghai is the location column, not an inference from the name. The figure is written undated because the table attaches no fiscal year to it. Deliberately not written: any owner, parent group, founding year or staff count. The firm's own site at smedi.com was not reachable through a search result, so it could not be opened; the Devex and DevelopmentAid profiles that searches return are barred by this brief; a Shanghai planning-bureau PDF and a conference sponsor page were the only other hits, the latter a sponsored featured-company page. This is my weakest entry: one trade-press ranking row, no ownership and no founding date.

codesc.name: Athi Water Works Development Agency
codesc.desc: Kenyan state water agency that develops and runs national public water works in Nairobi, Kiambu and Murang'a counties. Its own account is that it was established under the Water Act 2016 by Legal Notice No. 28 of 26 April 2019, as one of nine water works development agencies under the Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation, and that it also operates water works and supplies water until those assets are handed over to a county water provider.

sources.title: About AWWDA
sources.publisher: Athi Water Works Development Agency (Government of Kenya)

codesc.note: Opened the agency's own About page, which states 'established under the Water Act 2016 vide Legal Notice No. 28 of 26th April 2019', that it is one of nine Water Works Development Agencies 'established under the Ministry of Water, Sanitation & Irrigation', its functions ('Development, Maintenance and Management of National Public Waterworks'; 'Operate the waterworks and provide water services as a WSP until asset handover'; 'Provide reserve capacity'), and its area as Nairobi, Kiambu and Muranga counties. The 'sits under Y' claim is on that page and is written as the agency's own account. Deliberately not written: the page's 5,800.4 km2 and 9,320,287 population figures, which describe the territory and not the agency, and nothing is said about its predecessor the Athi Water Services Board, because the pages I opened do not state the succession: the Auditor-General's report on AWWDA for the year ended 30 June 2021 is catalogued in the Kenyan parliament library (item 85d9f2ae-fddf-4186-998c-477e2a9bd5db) but the catalogue record carries no institutional description and the PDF itself was not read. Note for the case data: the card's role text puts the agency under 'the Ministry of Water and Sanitation', while the agency's page gives the ministry as Water, Sanitation and Irrigation; the agency as named did not exist when the 2017 contract was signed, which the card already says by noting AidData names it in its earlier form.

codesc.name: China Gezhouba Group Corporation (CGGC)
codesc.desc: Chinese water-conservancy, hydropower and infrastructure builder, grown out of the bureau that built the Gezhouba dam on the Yangtze from 1970. It was listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997 and ceased to be listed in 2021, when China Energy Engineering Corporation Limited (Energy China) absorbed it by share swap, leaving it an unlisted joint-stock company. Its revenue was RMB 115 billion in 2020.

sources.title: CGGC of Energy China
sources.publisher: Belt and Road Portal, Government of China (eng.yidaiyilu.gov.cn)

codesc.note: Opened the Chinese government Belt and Road Portal's CGGC page, which names the company exactly as the case key does, 'China Gezhouba Group Corporation (CGGC)'. It carries the dated chain used above: construction of the Gezhouba dam begun 30 December 1970, renamed the 330 Engineering Bureau in 1974, the parent China Gezhouba Water Conservancy and Hydropower Engineering Group Corporation established 1994, listing on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997, main businesses fully listed by share swap in 2007, China Energy Engineering Group established 2011, and the 2021 acquisition and merger by Energy China that left it unlisted. The revenue figure is the one the page attaches to 2020 in the same passage (annual revenue RMB 115 billion, market contract amount RMB 300 billion, total profits RMB 8.6 billion). Deliberately not written: the page's 'national team' and 'global business card' phrasing, which is promotional, its 'over 5,000 projects' and '100 world records' claims, and the 2016 'revenue exceeded RMB 100 billion' line, which the page gives as a level sustained since rather than a year's figure. Caution recorded: this page treats CGGC and the Shanghai-listed China Gezhouba Group Co., Ltd. as one story, so the listing and delisting sentences are attributed to it rather than asserted of the corporation on my own account.
